name: Blind Image Quality Assessment (BRISQUE)
description: Evaluates the naturalness of an image without a reference by computing spatial domain statistics. AI-generated images or manipulated areas typically exhibit statistical deviations in their locally normalized luminance coefficients compared to authentic natural scenes.
mechanism: The algorithm calculates Mean Subtracted Contrast Normalized (MSCN) coefficients to normalize local luminance variations. In authentic photographic images, MSCN coefficients reliably follow a Generalized Gaussian Distribution (GGD). The method extracts 36 statistical features (shape, variance, spatial correlation) and uses a pre-trained Support Vector Regressor (SVR) to score the severity of unnatural distortions, including AI upscaling, synthesis blur, and compression artifacts.
parameters: Features: 36-dimensional MSCN parameters, Patch size: 7x7/9x9, Distribution fitting: Asymmetric Generalized Gaussian Distribution (AGGD), Classifier: SVR
accuracy: Moderate (70-80%) - Effective as a generic anomaly detector for unnatural noise, over-smoothing, or blurring.
source: Mittal, A. et al. (2012) - No-Reference Image Quality Assessment in the Spatial Domain
useCase: Flagging heavily processed, AI-upscaled, or synthetically generated content based on global statistical unnaturalness.

references.title: Mittal, A. et al. (2012). No-Reference Image Quality Assessment in the Spatial Domain. IEEE TIP.

strengths:
• Operates entirely in the spatial domain without requiring any pristine reference image.
• Computationally efficient and directly correlates with human perceptual quality metrics.
• Capable of detecting a wide variety of unnatural distortions and generative noise simultaneously.
• Works robustly on small image patches to map localized quality degradation or splicing boundaries.
limitations:
• High-quality AI generations from state-of-the-art models may perfectly mimic natural MSCN statistics.
• Often triggers false positives on screenshots, illustrations, or digitally native artworks.
• Does not identify the specific type of manipulation, only the presence of generalized spatial distortion.
• Requires strict domain-specific calibration to avoid errors when testing non-photographic inputs.
